title: Private state variables must have a leading underscore
description: Private state variables must be named with a leading underscore (`_varName`).

title: Internal functions and variables must have a leading underscore
description: Internal functions and state variables must be named with a leading underscore (`_funcName`, `_varName`).

title: Interfaces must be prefixed with `I`
description: Interface names must use a capital `I` prefix (e.g., `IFoo`, `IERC20`).

title: Non-standalone abstract contracts must use the `abstract` keyword
description: Contracts not intended to be deployed directly must be declared with the `abstract` keyword.

title: Unchecked blocks must be preceded by a safety comment
description: Every `unchecked` block must have a comment explaining why overflow cannot happen. The comment may be omitted if the reason is immediately apparent from the line above the unchecked block.

title: Custom errors should follow descriptive naming (no redundant `Error` suffix)
description: Custom error names should follow EIP-6093. Domain prefix order: (1) `ERC<number>` if violating an ERC spec, (2) component name (e.g. `Governor`, `ECDSA`). Avoid a generic `Error` suffix. Declare errors in: the underlying ERC if already defined there, else the interface/library, else the implementation, else the extension. Do not declare the same custom error name twice across the inheritance chain.

title: Overridable functions should be marked `virtual`
description: Functions intended to be overridden should be marked `virtual`. Exception: if A is purely an alias for B, only B needs `virtual`.

title: Order of functions within a contract
description: Functions must follow the order: constructor, receive, fallback, external, public, internal, private. Within each group, view and pure functions go last.

title: Modifier order on function declarations
description: Modifiers on function declarations must appear in order: visibility, mutability, virtual, override, custom modifiers.

title: Naming conventions for contracts, libraries, structs, events, enums
description: Contracts, libraries, structs, events, and enums must use CapWords. Functions, modifiers, arguments, and variables must use mixedCase. Constants must use UPPER_CASE_WITH_UNDERSCORES.

title: All import statements at top of file after pragma
description: Import statements must appear at the top of the file, after pragma statements.

title: File-level layout order
description: File-level elements must appear in order: pragma, imports, events, errors, interfaces, libraries, contracts.

title: Events must be emitted immediately after the state change they represent
description: Events should be emitted immediately after the state change they represent, and named in past tense. Exception: ERC standards using present tense (Transfer, Approval).

title: All state variables must be private
description: State variables must be private; state changes go through setters that emit events.

title: Use double quotes for strings
description: String literals must use double quotes, not single quotes.

title: Indentation: 4 spaces; spaces over tabs; no mixing
description: Use 4 spaces per indentation level. Spaces only — no tabs, no mixing tabs and spaces.

title: Blank lines: 2 around top-level declarations; 1 between contract functions
description: Surround top-level declarations with 2 blank lines. Between functions within a contract, use 1 blank line.

title: Maximum line length: 120 characters with specified wrapping format
description: Maximum line length is 120 characters. Long lines must be wrapped at specified break points.

title: Source file encoding: UTF-8 or ASCII
description: Source files must be encoded in UTF-8 or ASCII.

title: Whitespace in expressions: no extraneous whitespace inside parens/brackets/braces
description: No extraneous whitespace immediately inside parentheses, brackets, or braces.

title: Whitespace: no whitespace before commas or semicolons; no alignment spaces
description: No whitespace before a comma or semicolon. No extra spaces for alignment.

title: Control structures: opening brace on same line; `else` on same line as `}`
description: Opening brace of control structures goes on the same line as the declaration. The `else` keyword goes on the same line as the closing brace of the `if` block.

title: Mappings: no space between `mapping` keyword and its type
description: No space between the `mapping` keyword and its type (e.g., `mapping(address => uint256)`, not `mapping (address => uint256)`).

title: Array declarations: no space between type and brackets
description: No space between a type and its array brackets (e.g., `uint256[]`, not `uint256 []`).

title: Operator spacing: single space around operators; consistent on both sides
description: Single space on both sides of binary and assignment operators. Spacing must be consistent on both sides.

title: Within-contract layout order: type decls → state vars → events → errors → modifiers → functions
description: Within a contract, declare elements in order: type declarations, state variables, events, errors, modifiers, functions.

title: Names to avoid: never use `l`, `O`, or `I` as single-letter identifiers
description: Never use `l` (lowercase L), `O` (uppercase O), or `I` (uppercase I) as single-character identifiers — they are visually ambiguous.

title: Filename matching: contract/library name must match the filename
description: The filename must match the name of the contract or library it defines (e.g., `Foo.sol` for `contract Foo`).

title: Modifier naming: use mixedCase (e.g., `onlyBy`, `onlyAfter`)
description: Modifier names must use mixedCase (e.g., `onlyBy`, `onlyAfter`).

title: Naming collision: use `name_` trailing underscore to avoid reserved word clashes
description: When a name would clash with a reserved word, append a trailing underscore (e.g., `class_`).

title: NatSpec: fully annotate all public interfaces with `///` or `/** */`
description: All public interfaces must be fully annotated with NatSpec using `///` single-line or `/** */` multi-line style.

title: Numeric literals: hex for memory operations, decimal for bit operations
description: In assembly/Yul, use hexadecimal for memory locations, offsets, and lengths (e.g. `mload(0x40)`, `mstore(add(ptr, 0x20), value)`). Use decimal for shift amounts and bit positions (e.g. `shl(128, value)`). Trivially small values (1, 2) may use decimal even in memory operations.

title: Return values generally not named
description: Return values should not be named unless they are not immediately clear from context or there are multiple return values that need disambiguation.

title: Custom error names must not be duplicated across the inheritance chain
description: Do not declare the same custom error name more than once across contracts in an inheritance hierarchy, as this causes duplicated identifier errors when inheriting from multiple contracts.
